title: Define v7 decision-leg authority tables
description: Independent P1.4 prerequisite. Add isolated SQLite DDL for a one-row decision leg roster authority plus ordered per-leg bindings. The summary survives a missing-leg tamper and pins count/digest; the ordered rows bind expected fences and optional committed receipt digests. This slice proves the schema in isolation but does not bump or migrate the store yet.
definitionOfDone: DDL creates STRICT command_decision_leg_rosters and command_decision_legs tables with decision foreign keys, roster version/count/SHA-256 checks, contiguous safe leg indexes bounded by MAX_DECISION_LEGS, unique aggregate and receipt identities per decision, and all-null/all-present receipt digest constraints.
Real in-memory SQLite tests prove valid one-leg, committed three-leg, and no-business-effect null-receipt rows; foreign keys and every malformed/duplicate/out-of-range/mixed-null insert refuse.
Deleting or reordering a leg cannot mutate or delete the independent expected count/roster digest authority, and deleting a referenced decision/receipt is restricted.
Focused store tests run standalone with nonzero counts; mutation removing the summary table or uniqueness/check constraint makes a named assertion red.
taskRails: Do not bump SQLITE_SCHEMA_MANIFEST_VERSION/SCHEMA_VERSION or edit the live schema/migration in this slice.
Do not infer expected count or roster digest from command_decision_legs rows; the summary table is independent authority.
No legacy backfill is permitted here; a later integration row must refuse populated ambiguous v6 stores.

implementationPlan.description: Create packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-decision-legs.test.ts with the harness and the VALID arms (DoD 2's positive half). Use `DatabaseSync` from `node:sqlite`, the driver the store already uses. Build a helper that opens `:memory:`, creates the two FK parent tables (command_decisions and command_receipts — prefer the store's own committed schema SQL if exported per-object, otherwise minimal locals whose column names match exactly), then executes both statements from `SCHEMA_V7_DECISION_LEG_OBJECT_SQL`. THE HARNESS MUST `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` AND ASSERT IT: read `PRAGMA foreign_keys` back and expect 1, in its own named arm. That assertion is not ceremony — enforcement is OFF by default in a fresh DatabaseSync and every FK arm in step 2 is vacuous without it. Import MAX_DECISION_LEGS and DECISION_LEG_ROSTER_VERSION from their modules rather than hardcoding. Then the three valid shapes DoD 2 names: a one-leg roster plus leg; a committed three-leg decision with all receipt digests present; and a no-business-effect decision whose legs carry NULL receipt_command_id / request / effect together. Assert the rows read back exactly as written.

implementationPlan.description: Add the REFUSAL arms (DoD 2's hostile half) as a frozen case roster with an EXACT nonzero length assertion and member uniqueness, so a shrunken or emptied sweep cannot pass — a bare inline it.each literal is the vacuous sweep the global rail names. Each case asserts the insert THROWS and pins the constraint that refused it, not merely that something failed. Cover: roster_version not equal to DECISION_LEG_ROSTER_VERSION; leg_count 0 and MAX_DECISION_LEGS+1; roster_sha256 of wrong length and containing a non-hex character; leg_index -1 and MAX_DECISION_LEGS; expected_version negative and above 9007199254740991; a duplicate (decision_id, leg_index) against the PRIMARY KEY; a duplicate (decision_id, aggregate_id) against its UNIQUE; the same receipt_command_id reused across two decisions against the global UNIQUE; every MIXED-NULL receipt permutation against the all-null-or-all-present CHECK (command id set with either digest null, and each digest set alone); and the FK cases — a roster naming an absent decision, a leg naming an absent roster, a leg naming an absent receipt. Because the FK cases only mean something with enforcement on, gate them behind the step-1 pragma assertion.

On disk: REFUSAL_CASES is an Object.freeze'd roster ending at :504 with EXPECTED_REFUSAL_CASE_COUNT = 19 (:506) and EXPECTED_FOREIGN_KEY_CASE_COUNT = 3 (:507). The guard arm :510 asserts the count is > 0, that the roster has exactly that length, that all 19 names are distinct, and that exactly 3 cases carry requiresForeignKeys - so a shrunken or emptied sweep cannot pass. The sweep :518 pins WHICH constraint refused via kase.refusal fragments (CHECK_FAILED / UNIQUE_FAILED / FOREIGN_KEY_FAILED plus the constraint text built from the imported MAX_DECISION_LEGS and DECISION_LEG_ROSTER_VERSION), not merely that something threw, and re-asserts PRAGMA foreign_keys = 1 (:522) before each FK case. implementationPlan.description: Add the INDEPENDENCE and RESTRICT arms (DoD 3), which are the row's real point. Prove the summary is independent authority: with a committed three-leg decision in place, DELETE one leg row and assert the roster's leg_count and roster_sha256 are UNCHANGED — the schema must not silently re-derive them — so a missing leg becomes detectable by comparing the surviving leg rows against that independent count. Do the same for a reordering: rewrite leg_index values and assert the roster row is untouched. Then the RESTRICT arms: deleting a referenced command_decisions row while a roster references it must throw; deleting a referenced command_receipts row while a leg references it must throw. Use the `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` pattern already used at command-decision-leg-integrity.test.ts:312 and :396 ONLY where a tamper state must be constructed that the constraints would otherwise forbid, and turn it back ON before asserting.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED — writing or modifying DDL. It is delivered, clean and correct against DoD 1; rail 2 forbids bumping SCHEMA_VERSION or editing the live schema, and rail 1 restricts this row to three files of which the two source files already exist. This row owes proof, not code.

REJECTED — asserting DDL-level contiguity of leg_index. Not expressible in a per-row CHECK, not the DDL's job, and already owned by the landed codec row. An arm written that way would either be deleted in review or, worse, reported as a schema defect.

REJECTED — exercising the DDL through SqliteEventStore. Rail 2 says this slice proves the schema IN ISOLATION and does not bump or migrate the store. Opening the real store would drag in the live v6 schema and the migration path this row is explicitly not touching. Create the two tables directly in a scratch in-memory database instead.

DECISION ON PARENT TABLES, so the worker does not have to invent it: the two FKs point at command_decisions(decision_id) and command_receipts(command_id), which do not exist in a scratch database. PREFER creating those two parents from the store's own committed schema SQL if it is exported per-object the way SCHEMA_V7_DECISION_LEG_OBJECT_SQL is; fall back to minimal local parent tables ONLY if it is not, and in that case the column names must match exactly or the FK will not bind. Either way the plan requires a POSITIVE CONTROL proving the FK actually enforces before any FK refusal arm is trusted — an unbound or unenforced FK makes those arms pass while testing nothing.

Per the DELIVERY BIAS rail the plan is four steps: prove, drill, gate, record. There is no production change to TDD here, so the arms are written against already-correct DDL and their honesty is established by the step-3 constraint-removal drills rather than by a pre-fix red.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD ae83f365. The DDL half of this row is ALREADY DELIVERED; the proof half does not exist at all.

RAIL 1 NAMES THREE FILES TO CREATE. Two already exist, tracked and CLEAN (`git status --porcelain` empty for all three):
  packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-decision-legs.ts        TRACKED, 60 lines
  packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-decision-legs.js        TRACKED, 1-line bridge
  packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-decision-legs.test.ts   ABSENT — not tracked, not on disk

DoD 1 IS SATISFIED BY COMMITTED BYTES. I read the whole 60-line module. `SCHEMA_V7_DECISION_LEG_OBJECT_SQL` is a frozen object of two STRICT tables and every clause DoD 1 names is present: command_decision_leg_rosters has decision_id PRIMARY KEY, `roster_version` CHECK pinned to DECISION_LEG_ROSTER_VERSION, `leg_count` CHECK BETWEEN 1 AND MAX_DECISION_LEGS, `roster_sha256` CHECK on length 64 plus `NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'`, and an FK to command_decisions(decision_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT. command_decision_legs has `leg_index` CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND MAX_DECISION_LEGS-1, `expected_version` CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 9007199254740991, PRIMARY KEY (decision_id, leg_index), UNIQUE (decision_id, aggregate_id), UNIQUE (receipt_command_id), FKs to command_decision_leg_rosters(decision_id) and command_receipts(command_id) both ON DELETE RESTRICT, per-digest hex/length CHECKs, and the all-null-or-all-present receipt CHECK.

SO THE ENTIRE RESIDUAL IS DoD 2, 3 and 4 — the tests. There is no test file, so not one line of that DDL is currently proven. That is the whole slice and it is one file.

ONE THING THE DDL DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ENFORCE, so nobody hunts a phantom gap: CONTIGUITY of leg_index. SQLite CHECK constraints are per-row and cannot express "indexes 0..n-1 with no holes". The DDL gives range plus PRIMARY KEY uniqueness; contiguity is the CODEC's guarantee and it already landed in task-da09aa92d4a840d39ecc757df98abe70 (DONE), whose DoD 1 reads "contiguous zero-based indexes". Do NOT write an arm asserting the DDL refuses a sparse insert and then report a defect when it does not — assert instead that the roster's independent `leg_count` is what makes a sparse set detectable, which is rail 3's point.

SQLITE FACTS, measured not assumed:
- The driver is `DatabaseSync` from Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.ts:2 and sqlite-event-store-core.test.ts:4). No third-party dependency, nothing to add to any manifest.
- FOREIGN KEY ENFORCEMENT IS OFF BY DEFAULT. Production turns it on explicitly at sqlite-event-store.ts:184 (`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;`). A bare `new DatabaseSync(":memory:")` in a test does NOT inherit that, so every FK and every ON DELETE RESTRICT arm in this row is VACUOUS unless the test enables it. This is the single biggest correctness risk in the slice.
- Precedent for the inverse move exists: command-decision-leg-integrity.test.ts:312 and :396 and command-decision-integrity.test.ts:470 all use `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` to construct tamper states, which is a useful pattern for building states the constraints would otherwise forbid.

SIBLINGS ALREADY LANDED, so the surrounding authority exists and this row genuinely only owes proof of its DDL: decision-leg-roster.{ts,js}, decision-leg-roster-persistence.{ts,js}, decision-leg-roster-read.{ts,js}, decision-legs-contracts.{ts,js}, command-decision-leg-integrity.test.ts. `MAX_DECISION_LEGS` comes from decision-legs-contracts.js and `DECISION_LEG_ROSTER_VERSION` from decision-leg-roster.js — the DDL imports both, and the test must import them too rather than hardcoding their values.

GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/store test` resolves (@moe/store is packages/store) and `packages/store/package.json` sets `"test": "vitest run --root ../.. packages/store/src"`. The focused form used elsewhere on this board is `pnpm exec vitest run packages/store/src/<file>`.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE VACUITY TRAP, and it will silently pass if missed: `PRAGMA foreign_keys` defaults to OFF in a fresh `DatabaseSync`. Every FK and ON DELETE RESTRICT arm is meaningless without `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`. Enable it AND assert it — read `PRAGMA foreign_keys` back and expect 1 — before any such arm runs.
2. Import MAX_DECISION_LEGS and DECISION_LEG_ROSTER_VERSION from their modules; a hardcoded boundary detaches the moment either constant moves, which is exactly the assertion-drift the global rail names.
3. Do NOT assert DDL-level contiguity (see codebaseInsights) — it is the codec's guarantee, not the schema's.
4. Do NOT bump SQLITE_SCHEMA_MANIFEST_VERSION or SCHEMA_VERSION, and do not touch the live schema or migration (rail 2). Create tables in a scratch in-memory database only.
5. Do NOT infer expected count or roster digest from command_decision_legs rows (rail 3) — the summary table is independent authority, and DoD 3 exists to prove exactly that independence.
6. No legacy backfill here (rail 4); refusing populated ambiguous v6 stores belongs to the later integration row.
7. The test file is NEW and therefore UNTRACKED until committed, so `git diff` is a worthless drill-restore proof for it. The DDL file is tracked and clean, so `git diff -- packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-decision-legs.ts` empty IS valid there.
